subject.title: fix(browser): use public ssrf runtime import in CDP proxy bypass

question: Should the fix for the browser/Ollama `ssrf-runtime-internal` package-subpath regression preserve the private owner-scoped helper boundary, or promote the bypass helper into public `ssrf-runtime`?
rationale: The import-only patch is mechanically invalid, and the obvious way to make it valid changes a private SSRF/proxy helper boundary that current comments, package metadata, and guardrails keep private.

options.title: Preserve Owner-Scoped Helper Access
options.body: Keep the bypass helpers private and repair packaged Browser/Ollama resolution through the existing owner-scoped mechanism or another narrow private seam.

options.title: Approve Public SSRF Runtime Promotion
options.body: Promote the helpers only as an explicit SDK/security contract with docs, export metadata, guardrails, and package smoke proof.

options.title: Pick A Canonical Replacement
options.body: Pause this PR if maintainers choose a sibling PR or new replacement branch as the canonical repair for the same regression.

recommendation.title: Preserve Owner-Scoped Helper Access
recommendation.body: Keep the bypass helpers private and repair packaged Browser/Ollama resolution through the existing owner-scoped mechanism or another narrow private seam.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is package and Plugin SDK boundary policy, and this person has direct history on private SDK declaration/package hardening.
